changes: Share four query shapes by detail/aggregate mode and snapshot/period contract instead of eighteen per-dataset shapes
Keep the full nine-dataset catalogue and all business rules available on every interpretation
Validate dataset-specific fields, metrics, filters, having and sorting in Python after interpretation/refinement and independently in PHP
Retain compact JSON and bounded schema cache with independent request copies
Keep nonempty prior selections and the preceding question for follow-ups; place the current question last
Make authenticated-role restricted-field decisions explicit in prompt metadata
Use focused sampling for supported GPT-4.1/GPT-4o families; omit temperature only from the provider input-count endpoint
security_and_accounting: Backend remains authoritative for company isolation, live roles, module subscriptions and record permissions
No executable SQL or business result rows are generated by or sent to the model
Input counting, quota reservations, actual provider usage settlement, cached-token reporting and bounded validation retry remain in use
No database schema migrations or web/mobile UI changes required

checked: Present cohort retained through names and punch-in follow-ups
user_five_question_synthetic_conversatio.limits: Fictional selections only, without reading employee records. Comparison uses the user-reported old total, not replayed private production history. Generation latency excludes PHP execution, input-count preflight, rendering and downloads. Detail tables supply total_rows for combined count/list requests.

controlled_input_count_comparison.limits: Five fictional module questions measured before final follow-up instruction refinements. Uses provider exact input-count endpoint; full original catalogue supplied in both requests.

schema_preparation.limits: Local preparation only; first request is not warm-cached.

limitations: Token use varies by question, prior selection and a possible validation retry. Passing these checks does not guarantee every natural-language request is interpreted perfectly. Prior generic reference factoring/annotation stripping was removed; this implementation uses shared mode/date contracts plus runtime vocabulary validation.
privacy: Diagnostics used fictional questions, code-owned metadata and the five generic questions supplied by the user. No private history, employee results or delegated credentials were used.
